newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - May 5.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Monday:
POINTE NOIRE, Congo - Embattled Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila met for the first time amid signs that Zaire's civil war is rapidly coming to a close.
WASHINGTON - Washington, D.C. police officers are making more arrests for crimes they previously viewed as a low priority as part of Police Chief Larry Soulsby's "zero tolerance" crime initiative.

KRASNOURALSK, Russia - Children in this heavily industrialized region of Russia are suffering from chronic respiratory ailments and many have high levels of lead in their blood, which can lead to brain damage, mental retardation and behavioral problems.
SMELTERVILLE, Idaho - For nearly a century, a perpetual coating of toxic lead dust covered this former mining capital and now new cases of lead poisoning and damage are cropping up every day.

FORT DAVIS, Texas - A small band of Texas separatists who surrended to federal authorities Saturday had booby-trapped the area around their mountain headquarters with as many as 60 pipe bombs, tripwires and other explosives, investigators said.
WASHINGTON - Like an invisible gas, television is finding its way into nooks and crannies everywhere, including elevators, dentists' offices, and bank lobbies.
SEATTLE, Washington - Today, few tasks in public education are more difficult than stopping, even slowing, the exodus of middle-class parents and their children from urban public schools.
